title: Drain: accept unchanged-scope rereadings; ignore irrelevant config chang
summary: When athena.toml changes after a job was read, drain currently rereads each proposed item, gets a reading "needing accepting", records "no outcome", then wrongly retries a still-proposed job and stops on "repeated failure". Fix so that a config change not touching reading inputs (e.g. max_concurrency) doesn't invalidate readings, and a reread whose scope is unchanged is accepted and run by drain; the retry must only follow a rejected or failed job. Audience: the operator running unattended drains.

defaults_applied.how: Regression tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Fix both the over-broad invalidation and the drain's retry of a proposed job, not only the instance.
Criteria run the drain scenario and check landing.
One focused change in core run/capability and drain.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Enforced by tests rather than prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Scope equality means same capability, class_of_work and the same deliverable paths (action) in the new reading versus the one it replaces; probabilities and wording may differ.
Config relevance is decided by comparing a projection of the parsed config (excluding fields such as max_concurrency) rather than the raw file hash; defaults.toml changes still invalidate.
Acceptance by drain uses the existing AcceptedBy::Flag, as drain already passes it.
No change to athena.toml or defaults.toml is needed; the config change in the report was the trigger, not the fix.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs changes only max_concurrency in athena.toml after items are proposed/read; the drain lands them with no reread and no 'needs accepting' or 'no outcome' line. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain.

A test changes a reading-relevant config value (e.g. a budget cap or capability definition), so drain rereads; when the new reading has the same capability and deliverables as the old, drain accepts it and runs the job to a landed outcome in the same drain. Run: cargo test.

A test where the reread scope differs (different capability or deliverables) does not run silently: the drain leaves the item with a clear reason that the reading needs accepting, and does not stop with 'repeated failure'. Run: cargo test.

Drain never calls retry on a job that is still proposed: when a run ends with no outcome, the drain's next attempt is a run/accept of that job, not 'only a rejected or failed job can be tried again'. A regression test reproduces the 01:48 sequence (max_concurrency 1 to 2) and asserts the stop reason is not 'repeated failure'. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli.

Reading validity compares only the configuration inputs that bear on a reading; the existing test that a relevant configuration or defaults.toml change forces a reread still passes. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo test passes, cargo clippy --all-targets is clean, and cargo fmt --check passes.
Doc comments on GoResult::Reread and the reading-validity rule (D38) say what counts as a relevant config change and that a same-scope reread is accepted by drain; CHANGELOG notes the fix.

out_of_scope: Changing the retry rule that only rejected or failed jobs can be tried again
Changing interactive `athena go` acceptance behavior for readings whose scope changed
Changing drain budget or concurrency semantics
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass probability than reference: the change spans core and CLI and needs a drain regression scenario with config changes.
